results.summary: This design is a minimal neural processing unit with four parallel multiply-accumulate datapaths that computes a single fully connected layer with ReLU activation. It integrates custom arithmetic units generated by SproutHDL, including Han-Carlson multipliers and Sparse Kogge-Stone adders. A pipeline register between the multiply and accumulate stages ensures clean timing closure. The design stores weights and biases, runs pipelined inference in N_IN + 3 cycles, and is configured through command and data inputs.

It is designed for educational purposes and can be used to drive a seven-segment display. The design is purely combinational and does not require any clock. results.summary: This design implements a 64-point Radix-2 Single Delay Feedback Decimation-In-Frequency FFT in silicon, targeting the Tiny Tapeout 6x2 tile footprint. It requires an external controller, such as an FPGA or microcontroller, to generate the trigger sequence, send 64 data samples, and capture output samples. The interface is entirely synchronous digital, with 8-bit real input and 8-bit real and imaginary outputs, and no analog peripherals. The controller should also optionally reorder the captured bins by reversing their 6-bit indices for natural frequency order.

The documentation states only that it shows the Game of Life on the VGA board, with no details on resolution, timing, or control interface. The design uses a VGA PMOD that provides the VGA connector and resistor-ladder DAC. The output is a video signal that can be observed on a VGA monitor.
results.summary: FinSec-1 is a hardware-only AS-68M or AS-68ML fingerprint verification ASIC. It implements the complete AS-68M UART command protocol at 57600 baud, 8-N-1, as a 14-state deterministic finite state machine in synthesisable Verilog RTL, with no microcontroller, FPGA, or CPU in the trusted execution path. The design includes UART transmit and receive, finger-present input, and outputs for match, no-match, error, sensor-ready, finger-detect, UART-busy, and heartbeat signals. External hardware would include an AS-68M sensor and a UART host to communicate with the device.

results.summary: This design is a high-precision digital jitter meter that characterizes signal integrity in high-speed digital systems up to 50 MHz. It measures the temporal displacement of a target signal relative to a reference clock using a 17-bit synchronous counter running at 50 MHz. The core includes an arithmetic unit, a register bank for maximum and minimum jitter and sample counts, a UART protocol FSM, and a hardware gate pin to pause and resume measurements. It requires an external microcontroller and USB-to-UART adapter to configure parameters and retrieve results.
